programs.nl_rule:
The input grid contains several colored rectangular blocks arranged along the bottom rows, ordered from left to right with single-column gaps of black (.) cells between them. Each block is a solid rectangle of a single color. The rest of the grid above the blocks is entirely black (.).

1. Identify all distinct colored rectangular blocks in the input, ordered from left to right by their horizontal position. Note each block's width and height. 2. Place the blocks in a diagonal chain starting from the top-left corner of the grid (row 0, column 0). 3. Place the first block so its top-left corner is at (row 0, col 0). 4. For each subsequent block, position its top-left corner at the bottom-right corner of the previous block. The bottom-right corner is defined as (top_row + height - 1, left_col + width - 1) of the previous block — the next block's top-left goes exactly there. 5. Where two blocks share a cell (the overlap at the junction point), the later block's color overwrites the earlier one. 6. Fill all remaining cells with black (.).

The grid dimensions remain the same as the input (10x10). The background is black (.). Blocks are repositioned but retain their original shape and color.

The verifier identifies colors from bottom row unique nonzero left-to-right, extracts bounding boxes of each color (all positions with that val). Important nuance: blocks may not touch bottom? Actually arranged bottom rows. It extracts from bottom row order. Uses positions of color anywhere. If same color appears multiple disconnected? likely not. But we should teach that colors order by bottom row. Also note if block extends columns with zeros gaps.

Need decide demonstrations. We can show_transformed_input with random valid input. It will show gold output. The student learns from pairs. We can show multiple. Maybe start with simple: 3 blocks of distinct heights/widths. Then maybe overlap overwrite if later block's color overwrites at junction. Also cases with same? Distinct colors.

But expected top-left (4,0), h2 w4 -> rows4-5 cols0-3. Then 7 top-left at bottom-right of 2: (4+2-1=5, 0+4-1=3) -> rows5-9 cols3-4. Output rows5-9 cols3-4: row5 col3-4 are 7,7; rows6-9 col3-4 7. Overlap at (5,3) where 7 overwrites 2. Indeed row5 cols0-2 are 2, col3-4 7. So later overwrites.

Need maybe show a case with multiple overlaps maybe where later overwrites at corner. If blocks placed with h-1, w-1 increments, the overlap is exactly one cell? Actually next top-left = prev bottom-right, so overlap one cell? Let's check: next block includes cell at (r+h-1, c+w-1) which is prev bottom-right. Since next top-left same. Previous block includes that cell. So overlap one cell if next block placed starting there. Later overwrites. But if next block dimensions? Only one cell because next includes top-left; prev includes bottom-right. Unless there are further overlaps? No.

But note if a block's height or width 1, increment 0, so multiple blocks can share row/column and overlap more? Example h=1: next top-left row = same, col += w-1. Overlap one cell if w>1. If w=1 and h=1, increment 0,0, next top-left same as prev top-left, so entire next block (1x1) overwrites. But blocks likely at least? Could be 1. Need teach? Exam likely varied.

Let's consider verifier details: It extracts non_zero_vals from bottom row. It uses np.argwhere input==val for each val. If same color appears in multiple blocks, it would combine bounding box. But rule says distinct colored blocks. Exam likely distinct colors. It extracts bounding box, not connected component. So if a color has shape not rectangular? Rule says solid rectangles. Good.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.
